flawed_step: The claim overlooks the exceptional pair consisting of a triangle and a three-edge star.
counterexample: Let G=K3 with vertices {1,2,3} and edges {12,23,31}. Let H=K1,3 with vertices {c,a,b,d} and edges {ca,cb,cd}. Both graphs are finite, simple, and connected. In each line graph, all three vertices are pairwise adjacent: in G every two edges share a triangle vertex, and in H every two edges share c. Thus L(G)≅K3≅L(H). But G and H are not isomorphic, since G has 3 vertices and H has 4 (equivalently, their degree sequences differ).
assessment_summary: A concrete connected counterexample exists: K3 and K1,3 have isomorphic line graphs but are not themselves isomorphic.
